01:12 Amir: yeah I will, also question: does Redwood keep request-level logs in plaintext or are they redacted?
01:18 Owen: logs are stored with metadata, payloads can be redacted if you enable data retention controls and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest
01:26 Amir: okay need the exact KMS flow doc, and whether keys live in our account or in Redwood's KMS, that’s a blocker for audit sign-off

01:50 Leah: on the product side we ran some initial prompt tests, saw varying latency, wondering if the model variant choice could help
01:58 Owen: yeah the variant matters, we tested redwood-7b-quant and a 13b float on our small smoke test, quantized models give big cost savings but sometimes higher p90 in weird cases
02:12 Carlos: can you remind us of the tradeoff, like our SLO is p95 under 300ms for single-turn generation, is that realistic with quantized models?
02:22 Owen: with our serving runtime if your typical sequence length is short (<= 64 tokens), 7B quant is usually under 200ms p95 in our hosted region, but for multi-turn with long KV cache loads the 13B float maybe closer to 220-300ms depending on batch config
02:40 Priya: we care about both latency and cost, if dedicated capacity can give us predictable p95 that might be worth the commit
02:48 Maya: yep, we can do a sizing exercise, Owen can run benchmarks on hosted and on a dedicated node to show delta
02:56 Owen: plan: I will run an E2E benchmark with 1,000 prompts (the sample set Leah shared) on hosted and dedicated config, measure p50/p95, tokens/sec and cost estimate. will upload sheet to the bench doc link
03:10 Leah: thanks, the prompt set has a mix of short and medium sequences, might highlight tail latency
03:18 Carlos: any known infra gotchas? we were seeing some 502s in our smoke test yesterday

03:36 Priya: we saw an auth error that matched the timestamp, will share logs post-call
03:42 Owen: perfect, that will help narrow root cause, also double-check TLS and SNI if you're proxying through our gateway
03:50 Maya: on benchmarking, I'll send our bench template and a link to the preliminary hosted vs dedicated cost calc spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/nexa-2027 (note: placeholder link)
04:06 Amir: security follow up: can you confirm if audit logs include full prompts? we need to know retention and redaction options
04:14 Owen: prompts are treated as PII by policy if you toggle retention, default is 30 days and redaction off, but you can set automatic redaction or push to your KMS-backed bucket for archiving, we'll include details in the security doc
04:28 Carlos: good. also on network - we prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress, can Redwood support peering into our account in AWS and GCP?
04:36 Maya: yes, we support VPC peering and private link; specifics vary by region, Owen will coordinate with Priya on peering steps and CIDRs
04:46 Priya: for peering we'll need both sides' CIDR ranges and contact info for the cloud admin, I'll send a template for the peering request
04:54 Owen: noted, once peering is up we can switch traffic to the private endpoint and re-run the bench with internal routing to measure the delta
05:04 Leah: on model quality we saw a couple hallucinations on clinical templating, any recommended prompt engineering or filtering?
05:12 Owen: for clinical content we recommend instruction templates and safety filters, also consider a smaller reranker or a verification step post-gen. Redwood Optimize can surface prompt set regressions if you want continuous monitoring
05:26 Carlos: how much work to integrate Redwood Optimize? is it an add-on?
05:30 Maya: it's an add-on; we can enable a trial for the POC so you can see quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to your prompt set
05:38 Carlos: okay that would be useful, please enable trial and share how to onboard the prompt set
05:44 Maya: will do, action item captured
05:48 (brief silence)

06:12 Amir: on contract, can we get a carve-out for data residency and an SLA on deletion?
06:18 Maya: yes typical enterprise addenda cover residency and deletion with proofs, I'll have legal draft language and share it, will also include our data deletion process and audit trail notes
06:30 Owen: quick technical note - when we run the dedicated sizing we may suggest a multi-node pool if you have bursts, that helps keep p95 low while staying cost efficient
06:40 Priya: multi-node pool sounds good, we'll want autoscale rules that respect cost limits, can you share recommended autoscale thresholds?
06:48 Owen: yes, I'll include recommended autoscale settings in the sizing doc, e.g., target 60% GPU util, burst cap to 90% for short windows, and fallback to hosted in case of constraint
06:58 Maya: okay let's recap action items quickly: Owen runs E2E bench, Priya sends CIDRs, Maya shares security pack and pricing, Carlos to confirm success criteria, and we schedule sizing call
07:12 Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone
07:16 Maya: thanks all, I'll follow up in email with links and the bench spreadsheet, talk soon
